chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who releases his trained dog and says 'Bismillah' when he releases it. So he said: 'He may eat from what it holds for him. But if he reaches it before it dies, he should slaughter it. And if he finds an untrained dog with it, then he may not eat from it.'

So I said: 'And the leopard?' He said: 'When you come upon it while still alive to slaughter it, eat; otherwise, no.' I said: 'Is not the leopard in the same status as the dog?' So he said to me: 'Nothing is considered a trained hunting animal (mukallab) except the dog.'

key_terms.الْمُعَلَّم: Trained/taught animal; in fiqh, a hunting animal trained to chase and return prey without eating it
key_terms.ذَكَاة: Lawful slaughter; in hunting context, ritual throat-slitting to make game halal when still alive
key_terms.مُكَلَّب: A technical term for an animal trained for hunting (literally 'dog-trained'); in Shia fiqh, exclusive to dogs
key_terms.يُسَمِّي: Saying Bismillah at the moment of releasing the animal for the hunt — a required condition for lawfulness

ai.seo_question: Is hunting with a trained dog or leopard halal in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Abu Ubayda al-Hazza' asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the rulings for hunting with a trained dog, including conditions for permissibility of the game. The Imam specified that the prey is permissible if the dog was trained and Bismillah was said at release, but not if an untrained dog participated. When asked whether the leopard is legally equivalent to the dog for hunting, the Imam clarified that the term 'mukallab' (trained for hunting) exclusively applies to dogs — a technical jurisprudential principle that would have distinguished the Imam's school from other views.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Saalim, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib,f rom Abu Ubeyda Al haza’a who said, ‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who released (for hunting) his trained dog and he Named (Bismillah) when he released it. So heasws said: ‘He can eat from what it (dog) remains upon it. So when he comes over to it before it has killed it, he should slaughters it, and if he were to find an untrained dog with it, so he cannot eat from it’.

So I said, ‘So (what about) the leopard?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he comes over to it, he slaughters it, so he eats, or else, no’. I said, ‘Is not the leopard as the status of the dog?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘There is no trained hunting animal except for the dog’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from [Salim] and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘Ubaydah al- Hadhdha who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who sends his trained dog to catch a prey and mentions the name of Allah. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can use for food what the dog has caught and he must slaughter it properly, if he arrives at the site before the dog kills the prey. He must not use the catch for food if he finds a non-hunting dog with it.’

I asked about Cheetah. He (the Imam) said, ‘If you arrive in time to slaughter it properly then you can use it for food, otherwise, you cannot use it for food.’ I then asked, ‘Is not Cheetah like dog?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No other animals are called Mukallab (dogged, trained dogs) except dogs.’”
